doc.title: Ellen Rowe interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 2, 2024

title: Writing about Michelle Obama: 'Funky Yet Graceful' waltz
summary: Rowe describes thinking about admired traits in her subject and writing a waltz marked 'Funky Yet Graceful'.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Less dramatic perhaps. But so you’re going to write about Michelle Obama, do you have a process that before you even touch a keyboard or however you — do you think about the subject first and maybe come up with adjectives or themes to guide you?
Yeah. I think, in that piece I was just thinking about the aspects of her that I most admired and you know I don’t know that I’m consciously trying to go, you know, trying

to turn them into themes or things like that. But there was a definite — I think maybe the most telling thing is that you know it’s a waltz but on the top of the music for the players it says “Funky Yet Graceful.” And so I was trying to find something that had some blues elements in it, with chords that moved in slightly unusual ways for a jazz waltz. But also a certain grace in terms of things not being too herky jerky but things moving smoothly. So I mean I think that was kind of the approach on it was that I wanted to be somewhat sophisticated, as she clearly is, but also that you know soul and funk that she’s also known for. So that was kind of the thinking in putting that one together.
